MESSAGE 
2020

BIDV
  BIDV
Dear Customers, 
Investors and Partners,
2020 - the last year of this decade came to the 
end in contradiction with global expectation 
when the Covid-19 pandemic occurred. 
Never in the history had many countries 
experienced both economic and medical 
crisis which caused such severe socio-
economic damage. The Covid-19 pandemic 
became a shock and key impact that pushed 
the world economy into deep recession, 
besides recent major problems such as 
climate change, increasing protectionism, 
trade war, etc.
Vietnam became a rare bright spot in the 
gloomy global picture when the country 
fulfilled the dual goal of “effective pandemic 
prevention and socio-economic recovery 
and development”, among a few countries 
with the highest GDP growth of 2.91%. 
However, this is the lowest growth rate of the 
decade 2011-2020, resulting in economic 
difficulties and negative impacts on the 
operation of the commercial banking system.
Facing the disadvantages of the economy due to the impact of the unprecedented 
pandemic, BIDV showed its stuff and intrinsic strength of a leading bank, uniting to 
overcome difficulties, ensuring smooth operation with growth rate and business 
performance consistent with market movements. Looking back to 2020, BIDV’s total 
assets increased by 1.92 times compared to 2016, reaching VND1.52 quadrillion, 
becoming the largest bank by total assets in Vietnam’s banking system. Credit 
growth was at 8.5% compared to 2019, reaching VND1.23 quadrillion, increasing 
by 1.64 times compared to 2016, leading by credit market share, NPL ratio was well 
controlled. In the context of heavy damage to the economy, BIDV accompanied 
enterprises, proactively reducing income by more than VND6,400 billion to 
restructure debt, reduce interest rate, exempt interest and fees to support business 
and people to overcome difficulties, recover and grow business and production 
Obligations to the State budget, benefits of shareholders and employees are always 
ensured with the payment to the State budget of over VND6,400 billion, and cash 
dividend payout ratio in 2019 of 8%/year.
With achievements, the whole system of BIDV completed uniformly and 
comprehensively the targets of 2020 plan and the objectives of the Restructuring 
Plan for the period 2016 - 2020, giving effective support to national socio-economic 
development. BIDV continued to be honored with and awarded many domestic 
and foreign awards and titles such as: Top 2000 largest public companies in the 
world (Forbes), Top 300 most valuable banking brands globally (Brand Finance); 
awarded the title of national brand Vietnam Value for the sixth time; “Top 10 largest 
enterprises in Vietnam” for 4 consecutive years; Sao Khue Award 2020 for 6 excellent 
IT products.
Dear Customers, Investors and Partners,
2021 - the opening year of a new decade, new period of country’s development when technology has strong 
growth in the context of the global pandemic not been pushed back and social distancing everywhere changed 
economic patterns and human consumption behaviors, financial service needs to become more diverse... These 
offer both difficulties, challenges and opportunities for BIDV to continue its digital transformation in a stronger and 
more aggressive manner, aiming to be a leading financial institution in Southeast Asia, the bank having the best 
digital platform in Vietnam and the bank with the highest digital banking users.
With the motto of action “Discipline - Quality - Digital Transformation” BIDV is set to well implement plans, tasks 
and business plans in 2021 - the opening stage of implementing the strategy to 2025, with a vision to 2030. The 
whole BIDV system is determined to turn opportunities into driving force, difficulties into pressure, and advantages 
into resources and competitive strength for BIDV to promote the advantages of asset size, customer base, network, 
financial capacity, technology, workforce and 64 year tradition, affirming its leading position in Vietnam’s banking 
system.
On behalf of the Board of Directors, I would like to express my sincere thanks to all BIDV leadership and nearly 
26,800 employees for their dedication to the bank. Especially, I would like to extend my deep gratitude to our 
valued customers, investors and partners for their trust in and accompanying BIDV over the past time. BIDV wishes 
to receive your continued your cooperation and companion, looking forward to a sustainable and prosperous 
future!
May I wish you continued development and success. 
Sincerely!
ON BEHALF OF THE BOARD 
CHAIRMAN
Phan Duc Tu

Dear Valued Customers and Investors
Sustainable development on all three aspects of economy, society and environment is 
a global concern and an urgent requirement for Vietnam. Nowadays, economic growth 
is often associated with non-renewable natural resources (fuel, energy...), leading to 
the destruction of the natural environment, disruption ecological balance, causing 
catastrophic disasters. Sustainable development becomes a common responsibility 
of the whole society, requiring efforts and coordination from all economic sectors, 
regulators and social organisations.
The banking industry plays a role as an important capital channel of the economy, 
contributing significantly to the sustainable development of the country. A 
sustainable and efficient banking system will bring many benefits to the economy; 
minimize disadvantages to society and the environment.
Over 64 years of development and growth, BIDV has constantly accumulated and 
increased the sustainable development factors both in breadth and depth, both 
in terms of scale and scope of operations. As a leading bank in the country, BIDV 
defines our mission as: “Delivering the best benefits and conveniences to customers, 
shareholders, employees and society”
BIDV is aware that the harmonisation of interests between related parties including 
customers, shareholders, employees and the community is for the long-term 
existence of the bank. This also helps promote inclusive, long-term and sustainable 
growth that benefits the country’s economy and society.
BIDV’s perspectives on sustainability have been instilled into the entire organisation 
from the Board of Directors to each staff at all levels, from the overall strategy to 
implementation in each segment of business activities and products, service…
Sustainable Development Reporting is the practice of measuring, announcing and 
being accountable to all parties for their activities towards sustainable development. 
BIDV developed this Report to evaluate and disclose information about the Bank’s 
performance in environmental and social aspects, in addition to information on 
financial performance and governance. The report mentions three main focuses: (i) 
Sustainable economic growth; (ii) Investment in community development and (iii) 
Contribution to environmental improvement. As follows:
SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC GROWTH: For the banking industry, when referring to 
the sustainable aspect, we must first mention the financial sustainability to survive, 
develop in the long term, the balance between: the short and the long term; the 
expected profit and level of risk tolerance. The stability of a large commercial bank

SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE TRANSFORMATION
	 Continuing the achievements in implementing Rural 
Finance Projects, in 2015 BIDV was selected by the 
World Bank and the Government of Vietnam as the 
wholesale bank for Vietnam Sustainable Agriculture 
Transformation project (VnSAT).
	 The objective of the VnSAT project is to support the 
Government of Vietnam in promoting the “Agricultural 
Restructuring Project” through strengthening the 
institutional capacity of the agricultural sector; 
innovating the farming practice towards sustainability; 
continuously improving the value chain of the two 
product lines including rice and coffee in two key 
commodity production areas in Vietnam namely 
Mekong Delta (including 8 provinces: Kien Giang, An 
Giang, Hau Giang, Tien Giang, Long An, Dong Thap, 
Can Tho, and Soc Trang) and the Central Highlands 
(including 5 provinces: Lam Dong, Dak Lak, Dak Nong, 
Gia Lai and Kon Tum). Total IDA loans for the project 
were USD221.6 million, of which credit component 
was USD105 million implemented by BIDV and non-
credit component of USD116.6 million implemented 
by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development 
(governing agency).
	 Regarding credit component of the project, through 
a network of branches of PFIs, BIDV provided loans to 
end-borrowers who are individuals, households, and 
enterprises according to project’s eligibility criteria. 
As of 31 December 2020, with 10 participating PFIs 
(Agribank, Coopbank, OCB, VPBank, Techcombank, 
ABBank, TPBank, LVPBank, SHB, and Sacombank), BIDV 
completed the capital withdrawal and disbursed 
100% of credit of the project with total disbursements 
reaching VND2,599 billion. The credit component of 
the project had been completed on schedule, and 
the World Bank and the governing ministry highly 
appreciated the efforts and active activities of BIDV in 
the disbursement of the credit component in particular 
and the project in general.
	 The project has contributed VND4,965 billion of 
investment in the Central Highlands and the Mekong 
Delta regions (VND2,240 billion for rice and VND2,725 
billion for coffee), providing a stable amount of medium 
and long-term capital to coffee replanting people and 
rice processing enterprises, effectively contributing to 
the development of the agricultural and rural sector in 
these two regions. After the capital withdrawal period 
ended at the end of 2020, the project credit will be 
revolved by BIDV until 2040, continuing to contribute 
to supporting the development of the two rice and 
coffee industries according to the Project’s target.

during the implementation of the project since 2015

Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (the 
governing body of the VnSAT project) to research, 
develop and issue the “Environmental and Social

two books: Book 1 is for environmental and social 
management activities implemented by the Ministry 
of Agriculture and Rural Development and Book 2 is 
for environmental and social management activities 
carried out by BIDV. 
	 Based on the “Environmental and Social Management 
Framework (ESMF)” (Book 2) issued by the Minister 
of Agriculture and Rural Development in July 2015, 
BIDV actively realized the environmental and social 
management requirements into its “Project operational 
manual” - Volume 2 – Guidance on implementation 
of loans (POM2). On 4 February 2016, the Chief 
Executive Officer of BIDV signed Decision No. 740/
QD-BIDV regarding the issuance of the Credit activity 
implementation 
handbook 
applicable 
to

implementation of the entire credit component and 
details of environmental and social management 
procedures and processes according to regulations.

for implementing the Environmental and Social 
Management Framework (ESMF), BIDV monitored, 
provided guidance to participating financial institutions 
(PFIs) to comply with regulations on environmental 
and social safeguards according to provisions in 
the ESMF and POM2. During the implementation, 
BIDV reviewed, supplemented and amended POM2, 
revising provisions on environmental and social 
safeguards to match the actual implementation. As

plan

cumulative disbursements reaching VND1,834 billion.

replanting loans which satisfy all terms and conditions 
on environmental protection as specified in the ESMF 
and POM2.

environmental and social safeguards was carried out on 
a periodical and/or ad-hoc basis. During the monitoring

on regulations related to environmental and social

ACCOUNTING CONVENTION
The accompanying consolidated financial statements, 
expressed in Vietnam Dong (VND), are prepared under 
the historical cost convention and in accordance with 
Vietnamese Accounting Standards, accounting regime 
applicable to credit institutions in Vietnam and legal 
regulations relating to consolidated financial reporting. 
However, due to the Bank’s large scale of operations, for 
the purpose of preparing these consolidated financial 
statements, the figures are rounded to and presented 
in millions of Vietnam Dong (VND). This presentation 
does not materially affect the consolidated financial 
statements in terms of the consolidated financial 
position, the consolidated results of operations and the 
consolidated cash flows of the Bank and its subsidiaries. 
With regard to the number of shares and basic earnings 
per share, the Bank presented the items in unit as stated 
in Note 25 and Note 35.
The accompanying consolidated financial statements 
are not intended to present the consolidated financial 
position, consolidated results of operations and 
consolidated cash flows in accordance with accounting 
principles and practices which are generally accepted 
in countries and jurisdictions other than Vietnam.
BASIS OF CONSOLIDATION 
The consolidated financial statements incorporate 
the separate financial statements of the Bank and the 
financial statements of enterprises controlled by the 
Bank (its subsidiaries) for the year ended 31 December 
2020. Control is achieved where the Bank has the 
power to govern the financial and operating policies of 
investee enterprises so as to obtain benefits from their 
activities. 
The operating results of subsidiaries acquired or 
disposed of during the year are included in the 
consolidated income statement from the effective date 
of acquisition or up to the effective date of disposal, as 
appropriate. Where necessary, adjustments are made 
to the financial statements of subsidiaries to bring the 
accounting policies used in line with those used by the 
Bank. All internal transactions and balances between 
the Bank and its subsidiaries and among are eliminated 
in full on consolidation. 
Non-controlling interests consist of the amount of 
those non-controlling interests at the date of the 
original business combination (see below) and the non-
controlling interests’ share of changes in equity since 
the date of the combination. Losses in subsidiaries are 
respectively attributed to the non-controlling interests 
even if this results in the non-controlling interests 
having a deficit balance.

Provision is recorded in the consolidated income

CLASSIFICATION 
OF 
OFF-BALANCE-SHEET 
COMMITMENTS
The Bank classifies guarantee, acceptances of payment 
and unconditional, irrevocable loan commitments 
with specific effective date (collectively referred to 
as “off-balance-sheet commitments”) into groups as 
stipulated in Article 9, Article 10 or Article 11 of Circular 
02. Accordingly, off-balance-sheet commitments are 
classified by risk level as follows: Standard, Special 
mention, Substandard, Doubtful and Loss. 
INCOME AND EXPENSES
Interest and similar income expenses
Interest income and interest expenses are recognized 
in the consolidated income statement on the accrual 
basis. The accrued interest income arising from the 
loans that are classified from group 2 to group 5 in 
accordance with Circular 02 and Circular 09, accrued 
interest income on loans restructured and maintained 
in Standard loan group (group 1) as prescribed in 
Circular 01 and Decree No. 55/2015/ND-CP of 9 June 
2015 will not be recognized in the consolidated 
income statement. Accrued interest income on such 
loans is recorded as an off-balance-sheet item and 
is recognized in the consolidated income statement 
when it is actually received.
Interest income and interest expenses on investments 
in securities are recorded on the accrual basis. Accrued 
interest income of overdue securities is not recognized 
in the consolidated income statement for the year. 
Accrued interest income on such investments is 
recorded as an off-balance-sheet item and is only 
recognized in the consolidated income statement 
when it is actually received.
Insurance incomes and expenses
Direct premiums are recognized in accordance with 
Circular No. 50/2017/TT-BTC by the Ministry of Finance 
effective from 01 July 2017 (“Circular 50”). Accordingly, 
direct premium income is recognized when the 
following conditions are met: (1) the agreement has 
been entered into by the insurer and the insured, who 
fully paid premiums; (2) there is evidence that the 
contract of insurance has been signed and the insured 
has paid the premiums fully; and (3) the insurance 
contract is signed and there is an agreement between 
the insurer and the insured for delay payment of 
insurance premium, and in this case, the insurer will 
still record the premium amount as an income for the 
current year even though the amount has not been 
paid by the insured. The payment period is no longer 
than 30 days from the effective date of the insurance 
contract. 
In the case of the periodic payment, the insurer 
records income from insurance premiums of the first 
payment period when the contract is effective and 
only records revenue from insurance premiums of the 
next payment periods when the insured has fully paid 
the insurance premium as contract agreements. In case 
the insured has not fully paid the insurance premium 
according to the payment term, the insurance contract 
is automatically terminated at the end of the insurance 
premium payment term. The prepaid premium before 
the due date as at the consolidated balance sheet date 
is recognized in the “Other payables and liabilities” item 
in the consolidated balance sheet. 
Insurance claim expenses are recognized when the 
claim documents are completed and approved by the 
authorized person. In case that the final claim amount 
has not been finalized, but the insurer is certain that 
the loss is within its insured liabilities and has paid an 
advance to the customer as per their request, such 
advance would also be recognized as claim expense. 
The claims which have not been approved as at the 
consolidated balance sheet date are considered as 
outstanding claims and included in claim reserves.
The commission expense of each product is calculated 
as a percentage of the direct premium as stated in 
Circular 50. Commission expenses are allocated and 
recognized in the consolidated income statement 
corresponding with the premium earned.
Income from service charges and commissions
Income from service charges and commissions is 
recognized on an accrual basis.
Income from guarantee and L/C commitment 
activities
Income from guarantee and L/C commitment activities 
is recognized on the accrual and allocation bases. 
Recognition of dividends and profits received
Cash dividends and profits received from investment 
and capital contribution activities are recorded in the 
consolidated income statement when the Bank’s right 
to receive dividends and profits has been established. 
Share dividends, which are distributed from profits of 
joint stock companies, are recognized neither as an 
increase in the value of received shares nor financial 
income in the consolidated financial statements but 
are only used for tracking the increase in the number of 
shares according to Circular No. 200/2014/TT-BTC dated 
22 December 2014 issued by the Ministry of Finance.
Revenue from other service provision
When the contract results can be determined reliably, 
revenue will be recorded based on the level of work 
completion. If the contract outcome cannot be 
determined reliably, revenue will only be recognized at 
the recoverable level of recorded expenses.

EMPLOYEE BENEFITS
Post-employment benefits
Post-employment benefits are paid to retired 
employees of the Bank and its subsidiaries by the 
Social Insurance Agency under the Ministry of Labour, 
Invalids and Social Affairs. The Bank and its subsidiaries 
are required to contribute to these post-employment 
benefits by paying social insurance premium to the 
Social Insurance Agency at the rate of 17.5% of an 
employee’s monthly salary for their working period. 
In addition, the Bank also uses its Welfare Fund to pay 
one-time retirement benefits to employees under the 
Bank’s regulations.
Severance allowance 
According to Article 48 of Labour Code 2012, the Bank 
and its subsidiaries are responsible to pay severance 
allowance for employees who have regularly worked 
at the Bank and its subsidiaries for 12 months or more, 
half-month salary allowance for each working year 
before 01 January 2009. The working period used for 
calculation of severance allowance excludes the period 
that employees benefit from unemployment insurance 
and the working period that employees receive 
severance allowance from employers.
Retrenchment benefits
According to Article 49 of Labour Code 2012, the Bank 
and its subsidiaries are responsible to pay retrenchment 
benefits for employees who have regularly worked at the 
Bank and its subsidiaries for 12 months or more but are 
retrenched from their jobs as a result of organisational 
restructuring, 
technological 
changes, 
economic 
reasons, business combination, consolidation and split. 
For each year of employment, the employee is entitled 
to one-month salary but not less than two times the 
average salary of 06 consecutive months immediately 
preceding the job loss date. The working period used 
for calculation of retrenchment benefits excludes the 
period that employees benefit from unemployment 
insurance and the working period that employees 
receive retrenchment allowance from employers.
Unemployment insurance 
According to the Circular No. 28/2015/TT-BLDTBXH 
dated 31 July 2015 of the Ministry of Labour - War 
Invalids and Social Affairs guiding the implementation 
of Article 52 of the Employment Law 2013 and the 
Decree No. 28/2015/ND-CP of the Government dated 
12 March 2015 regulating the implementation of the 
Law on unemployment insurance, from 01 January 
2009, the Bank and its subsidiaries are obliged to pay 
unemployment insurance to eligible employees at 
1% of their salary fund allocated for unemployment 
insurance.
